lines_of_inquiry.detail: Three explicit viewpoints, each with named sub-claims. V1 task-level substitution CAPABILITY (C1.1 which tasks AI does faster/better; C1.2 adversarial: automation-substitution vs augmentation-complement). V2 job/employment-level NET change (C2.1 macro aggregates; C2.2 high-exposure occupations/cohorts; C2.3 adversarial: macro-cycle vs AI-as-label). V3 the core causal-identification puzzle lag-vs-genuinely-neutral (C3.1 GPT historical diffusion lag; C3.2 current deployment depth; C3.3 counter: effect already visible & accelerating; C3.4 counter: neutral camp, magnitude inherently small; C3.5 counter: lag & neutral not mutually exclusive / could be permanent). The problem is explicitly framed as three layers — capability, outcome, mechanism — with a stated 'diverge not decompose' method and a mandate to open at least one adversarial line per viewpoint.

leanings.detail: Every claim carries a '一句话结论' lean, every viewpoint a 汇总, plus a Root Conclusion holding the overall thesis. V1: task substitution is broad and growing but does NOT mechanically convert to net job loss (reinstatement + deployment friction buffer). V2: aggregates are mild, BUT a statistically robust, month-on-month widening net contraction is concentrated on the young-x-high-exposure entry-level slice; effect is localized, not economy-wide. V3: rejects BOTH strong extremes — not 'genuinely neutral/small' (effect is real and non-mean-reverting in the sharpest slice) and not 'pure lag/invisible in data' (already measurable; some independent methods give small magnitudes). Calibrated middle read: effect is real, directionally net-negative for specific groups, still 'small and concentrated' in aggregate as of 2025-2026, and structurally expected to grow as deployment deepens — i.e. we are on the early rising segment of a diffusion curve, not the terminal state.

key_figures.detail: Densely preserved with source tags. GPTs-are-GPTs (S3): 80% of US workforce ≥10% of tasks affected, 19% ≥50%; LLM alone accelerates ~15% of tasks, rising to 47-56% with tooling. ILO (S4): ~1/4 of workers have some GenAI exposure, framed 'transformed not redundant'. Macro (S7): unemployment 4.2% (Jun 2026), labor participation 61.5% (lowest since Mar 2021). Penetration (S8): only 17-20% of firms report AI use; big firms 37% vs small <20%. Stanford ADP (S1/S2): ages 22-25 in high-exposure jobs -16% relative employment (original), updated to -3.8%/yr shrinking ~0.5pp/month with no mean reversion; older cohorts stable/growing. Challenger (S6): 1.206M layoff announcements in 2025 (+58% YoY), 54,836 AI-attributed (~4.5%), hiring plans lowest since 2010. Indeed Hiring Lab (S13): post-2025 rebound skewed 71% senior, only 37% mention AI titles, software postings still -27.5% vs pre-pandemic. IMF (S5): high-AI-demand regions show high-exposure/low-complementarity jobs only ~3.6% lower after 5 years, plus AI-skill wage premium. Acemoglu (S10): ~0.7% TFP gain over 10yr, ~5% of tasks profitably automatable now. MIT NANDA (S9): 95% of GenAI pilots no measurable ROI; adjustment mainly via un-backfilled vacancies. Paul David electrification (S14): ~50% diffusion only by 1920s, ~30-year productivity lag.

adversarial_lines.detail: Adversarial lines are first-class and explicitly labeled, with rebuttals and residual-verdict calibration. C1.2: exposure = automation (net-negative) vs augmentation (complement) — Stanford Canaries + Acemoglu-Restrepo displacement vs reinstatement; verdict 'adversarial holds' (exposure ≠ net loss). C2.3: AI-attributed layoffs may really be macro cycle / tech-sector self-correction with AI as a label — critics Torsten Slok (Apollo) + Google economist attribute to rates/overhiring/remote-work unwind; Brynjolfsson rebuts that dropping the entire tech sector leaves the effect intact; verdict 'partly holds but not overturned'. C3.3: effect is already measured and accelerating, weakening the strong 'pure lag = invisible' version. C3.4: neutral camp's strongest evidence — IMF quasi-causal + Acemoglu structural both give single-digit-% magnitudes. C3.5: epistemological caution — 'will show up in a few years' vs 'this is the real long-run effect' cannot be separated by waiting; needs mechanism evidence (deployment/pilot-failure rates).

The sources/ directory contains S1.txt-S14.txt — a 1:1 match to all 14 citation tags — so each claim's backing source snapshot is on disk and independently checkable.
